 Learn more Nvidia ( NVDA ) reported its Q3 results after the bell Tuesday, beating Wall Street's expectations on the top and bottom lines and offering a better-than-anticipated Q4 outlook. The company also announced a $150 billion stock buyback. Nvidia stock rose on the news. 
 For the fourth quarter, Nvidia expects revenue between $127.4 billion and $132.6 billion. Analysts were anticipating $125.25 billion 
 For the quarter, Nvidia saw earnings per share of $2.68 on revenue of $115.8 billion. Wall Street analysts were projecting EPS of $2.47 and revenue of $109.15 billion, based on Bloomberg consensus estimates. 
 ( NVDA )
 Go deeper with AlphaSpace 155.46 -0.68 (-0.44%) At close: 4:00:00 PM EST 159.08 +3.62 (+2.33%) After hours: 4:28:36 PM EST The company reported EPS of $1.30 and revenue of $57 billion in Q3 last year. 
 Data Center revenue topped out at $107.6 billion versus an anticipated $101.85 billion. The company's Edge Computing segment brought in $8.2 billion versus an expected $7.49 billion. 
 This is Nvidia's first earnings report since CFO Colette Kress took over as interim CEO, following Jensen Huang's resignation last week. 
 Huang left the company after revelations regarding a series of affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy and another with an alleged Nvidia employee. 
 LIVE 31 updates 12 mins ago Grace O'Donnell SEC is investigating Nvidia, Wall Street Journal reports
 As Nvidia prepares to report earnings, the Wall Street Journal is reporting that the Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating the company, according to people familiar with the matter. 
 The full purpose of the investigation wasn't known, but it does involve the company's disclosures and whether they misled investors, the report said. 
 The investigation marks the latest headache for the AI chipmaker in the wake of founder Jensen Huang's affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese agent, and his resignation from the company, which has created significant uncertainty for the company. 
 The Justice Department is now leading investigations into Huang's relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. Shareholders have also filed a class-action lawsuit, alleging Jensen Huang misled investors about his affair with Alice Huang. 
 Before Jensen Huang admitted to having an affair, Nvidia denied that there was anything "unusual or unexpected" about his relationship with Alice Huang. 
 42 mins ago Ines Ferré Huang's plea to return to Nvidia 'moves the fight from a petition to the board'
 Jensen Huang's statement that he would be "honored" to return as CEO of the AI chip giant he co-founded, if the board determines it is in shareholders' best interests, sets the stage for a growing battle over the company's future. 
 In recent days, SpaceX ( SPCX ) and Tesla ( TSLA ) CEO Elon Musk has publicly backed Huang, saying he signed a petition calling for his reinstatement. President Trump has also voiced support for Huang's return, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has argued that an outsider should take the job. 
 "Clearly Jensen wants to come back as CEO, and the statement moves the fight from a petition to the board," Yorkville's Dan Ives said Tuesday. 
 "The board will get more pressure from here, and activism could play a role," he added. 
 Ives noted that Nvidia's bylaws allow shareholders who have held at least 15% of the company's stock continuously for at least one year to call a special meeting. Given Nvidia's roughly $4 trillion market value, that would likely require a coalition of its largest index and long-only investors. 
 "Every director stands for election annually on a majority vote, so a special meeting would not just be a referendum on Jensen; in our view, if the board that removed him does not engage with its shareholder base, the board itself could be the one actually voted out if this plays out, " he added. 
 44 mins ago Daniel Howley Nvidia earnings on deck. Here's what to expect. 
 Nvidia will report its third quarter results after the bell on Tuesday, its first major public event since former CEO Jensen Huang stepped down amid an affairs scandal. 
 Interim CEO Colette Kress, the company's CFO, will host the call, during which she'll likely address the matter, though she'll likely go into little detail. 
 Nvidia's stock price has taken a serious hit since the Huang scandal broke out and is now down nearly 17% year-to-date. 
 Analysts across Wall Street have responded to the shake-up by lowering price targets on or downgrading Nvidia's stock. While the consensus is that the company is in good hands under Kress for the time being and that sales are already locked in for next year, there are also questions about the company's long-term outlook. 
 For the third quarter, Nvidia is expected to report earnings per share (EPS) of $2.47 on revenue of $109.15 billion, up from $1.30 and $57 billion in Q3 last year. 
 Data Center revenue is projected to peak at $101.85 billion, with Hyperscale bringing in $53.61 billion and AI Clouds, Industrial, & Enterprise at $48.64 billion. 
 Nvidia's Edge Computing business, which includes everything from gaming chips to automotive technology, is expected to generate $7.49 billion in sales.

 George Soros's family office, Soros Fund Management, cut its Nvidia holdings during Q3. Yahoo Finance anchors discuss the move. 
 Today at 8:00 PM UTC Jared Blikre Nvidia earnings will show if the Bank of Nvidia is still open
 Nvidia reports Tuesday with its longtime finance chief, Colette Kress , in charge. The Bank of Nvidia she inherited was already turning customers away. 
 Wall Street will grade Nvidia ( NVDA ) on chips and guidance after the bell . But the most revealing page may sit in the back of the filing, where Nvidia lists what it has promised to pay or guarantee for others. 
 That list nearly doubled in a single quarter, JPMorgan's Michael Cembalest noted , and comes to about $530 billion with guarantees included. Huang's exit put that web of deals under the microscope. 
 The man who built the bank had already started closing its windows. 
 Steps Nvidia took to rein in financing for AI customers, 2026 · The Wall Street Journal, Reuters, Nvidia, Yahoo Finance Neoclouds may be rooting for a Huang comeback , but his return wouldn't reopen windows he was shutting himself. Kress is expected to tighten the purse strings even further, the Journal reported. The $500 billion lending platform Nvidia launched with Wall Street in August still hasn't closed a deal, and lenders want Nvidia to back more than a quarter of each loan, Bloomberg reported. Read More . 
 Today at 7:30 PM UTC Yahoo Finance Yahoo Finance anchors discuss Nvidia's new export control committee 
 Yahoo Finance's "8:30" show hosts break down Nvidia's new oversight committee. 
 Today at 7:00 PM UTC Why Nvidia may need an operator as CEO — not a visionary
 Siebert Financial chief investment officer Mark Malek and his panel of experts weigh in on what type of CEO Nvidia ( NVDA ) needs. 
 Today at 6:30 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Kevin O'Leary: Colette Kress is exactly who Nvidia needs — not Jensen Huang
 If "Shark Tank" host and investor Kevin O'Leary were on Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board, he would be in no hurry to bring Jensen Huang back into the fold. 
 "It probably will never happen because … [of] the amount of scrutiny this company is going to go through during this administration's microscope on it for the whole Chinese issue," O'Leary said on Sozzi Unleashed about the possibility of Huang returning. "You have so many agencies launching investigations domestically and internationally. I mean, you've got Treasury and Commerce at loggerheads right now. There's just too much noise to make that move." 
 O'Leary still considers Huang a genius entrepreneur. But he stated that Huang's genius is "not what the company needs right now." 
 "It's got to get somebody that can deal with all of this," O'Leary said. "People are saying to me, who do you think that should be? I don't think you should bring in anybody in from the outside. I think you got what you need right now in Colette [Kress]." 
 Interim CEO Kress will have her first big moment after the bell when she hosts Nvidia's earnings call. 
 "Let her run with it for a few quarters and see how she operates," O'Leary said. 
 Today at 6:00 PM UTC Yahoo Finance Nvidia warns chip buyers of legal risks tied to China AI access: CNBC
 Sources told CNBC that Nvidia warned customers that a new law could expose them and the chipmaker to "legal action" over Chinese access to chip capacity. 
 Current US controls restrict shipments of advanced chips to China, while Congress is considering broader authority over remote access to chips hosted in overseas data centers. 
 Nvidia said it would not sell its chips to customers who rent more than 50% of their graphics processing units (GPUs) to Chinese companies. 
 Today at 5:30 PM UTC Yahoo Finance Nvidia's Colette Kress faces some serious pressure head of Q3 earnings: YF executive editor Brian Sozzi 
 Yahoo Finance's executive editor weighs in on the challenges facing Colette Kress, Nvidia's CFO and interim CEO, ahead of earnings today. 
 Today at 5:00 PM UTC Brian Sozzi Opinion: Should Nvidia bring Jensen Huang back, as Silicon Valley's elite are demanding?
 Something pretty remarkable is happening in Silicon Valley right now. One shouldn't be surprised, considering the profit motives of many invested in the AI ecosystem and that what Nvidia ( NVDA ) does lies at the center of it all. 
 Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigned as the company's CEO under a cloud of controversy he created, and suddenly some of the biggest names in Silicon Valley are organizing a campaign to bring him back. 
 The online petition has attracted more than 180,000 signatures. Nvidia employees have also taken to X and LinkedIn to voice their support for Huang. 
 Let's be clear: Jensen Huang is an extraordinary entrepreneur . A once-in-a-lifetime type of talent. He helped build Nvidia into one of the world's most important companies, with a market cap that neared $5 trillion earlier this year. His impact on the AI revolution is enormous and will not be forgotten. 
 FILE PHOTO: Jensen Huang reacts to a video at his keynote address at CES in Las Vegas, Nevada, U.S. January 7, 2018. REUTERS/Rick Wilking/File Photo · Reuters / REUTERS But here's the issue a lot of people are right to point out: Being a brilliant CEO does not make you untouchable. 
 This isn't just about one man's personal life. It's about corporate governance, national security, the responsibilities of a CEO, and the standards expected of someone running one of America's most strategically important companies. 
 Nvidia's board has a responsibility to shareholders, employees, and the country — not to Silicon Valley's celebrity CEO culture. 
 Jensen Huang absolutely deserves due process. But he is not bigger than Nvidia. And no CEO, no matter how brilliant, should be. 
 Today at 4:59 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Nvidia stock yo-yos after Jensen Huang floats comeback
 Nvidia ( NVDA ) stock is swinging as investors digest Jensen Huang's first public statement since his ouster. 
 On Tuesday morning, the stock sank over 3%. After Huang said he'd be willing to come back (see my colleague Dan Howley's blog below for the full statement), the stock nearly recovered entirely from those losses. 
 But it didn't hold. Nvidia shares have fallen again and are down 2%, as it's clear there's no easy way forward for the company or Huang.

 Today at 4:36 PM UTC Daniel Howley Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says he'd be 'honored' to return to the company 
 Former Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang says he would be "honored" to return as chief executive of the company he cofounded. 
 In a statement Tuesday, Huang apologized to his family again and commented on the support he's seen among former employees, customers, and others seeking to have the company's board reinstate him, The Wall Street Journal reported . 
 A person familiar with the matter told Yahoo Finance that Nvidia's board is not looking to bring Huang back. 
 Read more here. 
 Today at 4:00 PM UTC Yahoo Finance Could Jensen Huang launch a new startup within six months?
 Market Hang host Mark Malek, Siebert Financial's chief investment officer, and his panel of experts weigh in on whether Jensen Huang will start a new venture. 
 Today at 3:52 PM UTC Ines Ferré Jensen Huang to appear before congressional committee on Dec 1
 Former Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang will appear before the US House Foreign Affairs Committee on Dec. 1, the committee ​said in a statement on Tuesday. 
 Huang resigned as CEO last Thursday following reports of extramarital affairs, including an alleged relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Scrutiny has grown over concerns about Chinese access to the company's advanced AI chips. 
 The transcribed interviews will also be before the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and the House Intelligence Committee, according to the statement. 
 Nvidia's General Counsel will appear before the congressional committee on Dec. 2. 
 Today at 3:38 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Nvidia founder Jensen Huang's departure is 'horrible' for neocloud companies: Analyst
 One thing we're watching as the Jensen Huang controversy continues to unfold is the fallout not only at Nvidia ( NVDA ) but also across the network of companies caught in the AI chip king's web. 
 And one industry that could face a dark cloud is the neocloud space, as AI-focused compute companies like CoreWeave ( CRWV ) have lost their champion in Huang. 
 Niles Investment Management founder and portfolio manager Dan Niles told Yahoo Finance he thinks Jensen Huang's exit as CEO is "horrible" for neoclouds. 
 Niles noted that interim CEO Colette Kress, who served as CFO for many years before her recent promotion, is going to more closely examine all the deals that Nvidia has made. 
 "She wasn't as big of a proponent for that and all the circular financing," Niles said about Nvidia funding the AI ecosystem. He added that the so-called Bank of Nvidia will be "slammed shut shortly, and we'll have to see where the world shakes out from that." 
 Watch the full interview below: 
 Today at 3:00 PM UTC Brian Sozzi Jensen Huang looks to have accepted his fate with Nvidia: He cleaned up his X profile
 Jensen Huang appears to be accepting that he will not be returning to Nvidia ( NVDA ) as CEO. 
 At least, that's if you decode the move he just made on his X account. 
 Huang updated his profile on Tuesday, changing it to simply "founder" of Nvidia. It no longer has the Nvidia affiliation badge. 
 Today at 1:58 PM UTC Hamza Shaban Nvidia is being pulled in opposite directions by 2 powerful forces
 Everyone's social feeds are a little different. So depending on your own views towards China, open-weight AI models, Silicon Valley founders, and the role of Big Tech in society, the idea of Jensen Huang returning to Nvidia ( NVDA ) is a brilliant, righteous comeback, a threat to national security, or the height of corporate irresponsibility. 
 Nvidia is reportedly waving off the comeback. Its efforts are directed instead to the investigation into Huang and navigating a regulatory landscape that's more hostile to Chinese competition. But regardless of the company's public posture, it is being pulled in opposite directions by very powerful forces. 
 Much of the tech world is clamoring for Huang's return. Meanwhile, members of Congress are sharpening their oversight knives. And in an extraordinary show of Cabinet infighting, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent accused Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick of failing to block China from getting ahold of Nvidia's most advanced chips. 
 Part of what has made Huang's reported affairs and resignation such a big story is that the saga contains so many competing storylines . Read more . 
 Today at 1:36 PM UTC Yahoo Finance US releases details of Megaspeed probe, says investigation began in 2024
 Reuters reports that the US Commerce and Justice Departments have been investigating Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed, Nvidia's Asia-Pacific partner, at which Alice Huang was an executive. Huang is an alleged Chinese spy and had an extramarital affair with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. 
 "After identifying suspicious activity through proactive monitoring of potential sensitive semiconductor diversion, the Department of Commerce initiated an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations," the two agencies said in a joint statement. 
 In May 2025, Department of Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia concerning direct or indirect sales ‌to Megaspeed and in June 2025 Nvidia placed Megaspeed ⁠on its "no sell" list, the joint statement said. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside regular business hours. 
 US agents, in conjunction with Singaporean law enforcement officials, ⁠conducted an "on-site, in-person, end-use check at Megaspeed" in June 2025 and interviewed Alice Huang, who was then CEO, the Commerce and Justice Departments said. 
 Following the enforcement action, the Justice Department took the lead role in a criminal investigation into Megaspeed, the statement added. 
 The ​statement said ​that while US agencies typically did not comment on ongoing ​investigations, on this occasion the details provided were ‌in the public interest." Read more. 
 Today at 12:49 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Nvidia's board establishes national security and chip export oversight committee amid heightened scrutiny
 Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board of directors is setting up a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, the company announced Tuesday as it looks to rebuild its reputation following a scandal that raised questions about the company's oversight into chip smuggling into China. 
 Nvidia said the new standing committee will meet quarterly and be responsible for overseeing the company's national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risk management. Nvidia's existing National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team will report to this committee, as well as new CEO Colette Kress. 
 "NVIDIA recognizes that advanced silicon technologies and the emergence of artificial and superintelligence present unprecedented challenges for national security," Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones said in a statement. "We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation." 
 The announcement comes as Nvidia has faced greater scrutiny on its China ties in the wake of former CEO Jensen Huang's affair with Megaspeed executive and suspected Chinese agent Alice Huang. Reports have also suggested that Nvidia benefited from a loophole in US chip export curbs that allow Chinese companies to use Nvidia-powered compute remotely from data centers in other Southeast Asian countries. 
 On Monday, the Trump administration advanced new limits on chip exports that would work to close that loophole. 
 Nvidia reports earnings after the bell.
